summary_html: The child is **removed from the home** and placed in foster care under court order or emergency authority. Federal statutes tie funding to safety findings, judicial oversight, and permanency planning.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: R.F. v. Florida Department of Children & Families
key_cases.holding: Proof that a parent sexually abused one child does not by itself establish that a sibling is dependent; the court must examine all the circumstances to decide whether the parent poses a substantial risk of imminent abuse or neglect to the other child.
key_cases.relevance: Removal and foster placement of an unharmed sibling requires case-specific proof of substantial risk, not a per se rule.
key_cases.quote: While the commission of such an act may be highly relevant, it is not automatically dispositive of the issue of dependency.

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit
key_cases.holding: Florida's emergency removal statute comports with due process, and the caseworker was entitled to judgment because the circumstances showed an objectively imminent danger to the children justifying removal without prior court authorization.
key_cases.relevance: The constitutional test in Kearney governs the removal that precedes any foster placement.
key_cases.quote: there was an objectively imminent danger to the Doe children so as to justify O'Brien's temporary removal of the children without prior court authorization

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit
key_cases.holding: In a systemic challenge to Florida's foster care system, standing must be shown claim by claim; some plaintiffs' claims were moot and others were dismissed for lack of standing, leaving only counts for which a particular plaintiff demonstrated injury in fact.
key_cases.relevance: The claims concerned conditions, safety and case planning for children already in Florida foster placements.
key_cases.quote: Only Reggie B. has standing to pursue the procedural due process claims set out in Count II, because he is the only plaintiff who has demonstrated injury in fact

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: Illinois could not presume unwed fathers unfit and make their children wards of the State without a hearing; due process entitled Stanley to a hearing on his parental fitness, and denying him the hearing afforded all other parents denied him equal protection.
key_cases.relevance: Children may not be placed with court-appointed guardians on a statutory presumption of unfitness; the placement must follow a fitness hearing.
key_cases.quote: as a matter of due process of law, Stanley was entitled to a hearing on his fitness as a parent before his children were taken from him
